close_reason: Done in aae60b4. Added 'Do not remove the cap' section to MAX_CONSECUTIVE_NON_TEXT_FRAMES rustdoc enumerating five reasons the cap is load-bearing. Defends against bd:JMAP-6lsm.6 regression.
description:
ws/mod.rs:120 defines MAX_CONSECUTIVE_NON_TEXT_FRAMES: usize = 64 and the next_frame() loop at lines 166-206 counts consecutive Ping/Pong/Frame messages, returning UnexpectedResponse after 64.

A contributor may suggest 'tungstenite handles pings at the protocol layer, just continue the loop silently for any non-text non-close frame.' That removes the cap and reintroduces the bug bd:JMAP-6lsm.6 fixed.

Defense:
1. A hostile or misbehaving server can flood the WebSocket stream with no-op frames (Ping, Pong, Frame, future variants) and starve a caller of next_frame() indefinitely. The cap surfaces this as an error before the caller's outer loop is starved.
2. 64 is high enough that a normal connection never trips it (typical WS streams interleave at most a handful of pings between data frames). Lower numbers (e.g. 8) would produce false positives on networks with weak NAT keepalives.
3. Binary frames are explicitly NOT counted — they violate RFC 8887 §4.1 and surface immediately on first occurrence (ws/mod.rs:185-193). This is a separate guarantee, not subsumed by the cap.
4. The classify_message function (line 128) is extracted as a free function so the policy is unit-testable without a real WebSocket — the test suite at line 600+ exercises the classification explicitly.
5. consecutive_skip_cap_matches_documented_value (line 649) is a tripwire test that fails loudly if the cap is retuned, forcing a deliberate choice.

This is defense against a class of resource-exhaustion attack that's invisible on happy-path testing. Resist requests to 'simplify' by removing the count.
title: WebSocket consecutive-non-text-frame cap of 64: defend against 'tungstenite handles pings, just skip them silently'
